items.title: Image+
items.text: Image+ is an advanced image template variable for MODX. The dimensions for the uploaded image can be configured (optionally) to restrict a minimum width and/or height. Image cropping can be forced to stay within a preset ratio. A graphical tool can be used to resize the image to the desired dimensions/proportions.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• MODX Revolution 2.8+
  • PHP 8.2+
  • Optional: pThumb for further image processing in the output chunk

items.title: Features
items.text:
• Visual tool for cropping images, integrated with MODX Manager interface.
  • Option to restrict minimum width and/or height for uploaded image.
  • User image cropping can be forced to stay at preset ratio.
  • Use chunk as output mask and fill placeholders with url, height, width, alt tag etc. of the image crop file.

items.title: Examples
items.text: Image+ can be used for various purposes. On this page you will find some examples of how it can be used:

items.title: Collections
items.text: You can display the Image+ thumbnail in a column of the Collections grid by setting the column's renderer to ImagePlus.ColumnRenderer.

items.title: MIGX
items.text:
If you want to use Image+ in MIGX, you can configure all Image+ TV properties with a JSON string in the Configs textarea in the MIGX formtabs field. The following properties are possible:

{
    "sizes":"",
    "minWidth":"",
    "minHeight":"",
    "format":"",
    "uploadPath":"",
    "thumbnailHeight":"",
    "inlinePreview":"",
    "allowAltTag":"",
    "allowCaption":"",
    "allowCredits":""
}

You also need to change the Input TV Type to imageplus.

You can display the thumbnail in the grid column by setting the renderer to ImagePlus.ColumnRenderer. In earlier versions of MIGX, you need to edit a MIGX configuration to do this.

To use this Image+ MIGX field in the frontend, call the ImagePlus Snippet where the value parameter is the name of the MIGX field. If the MIGX field does not use the default media source, set its ID with the source parameter:

[[ImagePlus? 
&value=`[[+migxImagePlusField]]`
&source=`2`
]]

This will give you the prepared URL for the cropped image instead of the raw JSON object.

items.title: getResources/pdoResources
items.text:
In order for the TV to be parsed using the getResources/pdoResources snippet, you need to add the following lines to your getResources/pdoResources Snippet call:

&includeTVs=`name_of_your_tv`
&processTVs=`name_of_your_tv`

In the template chunk of the getResources/pdoResources snippet call, you can use the placeholder [[+tv.name_your_TV]] if the TV's Output Type is set to Image+. Without any further changes, the placeholder will contain the URL of the cropped image.

items.title: Using the ImagePlus snippet in the getResources/pdoResources template chunk
items.text:
In your template chunk for calling getResources/pdoResources Snippet, you need to add a parameter so that the ImagePlus Snippet call knows the origin ID from which to retrieve data:

&docid=`[[+id]]`

Here is an example of a call and configuration, where image is your Image+ TV:

Snippet Call 

<div class="blog-articles">
[[!pdoPage?
    &element=`pdoResources`
    &tpl=`tplBlogPost`
    &limit=`11`
    &includeContent=`1`
    &showHidden=`0`
    &hideContainers=`1`
]]
</div>
<div class="blog-paging">
  [[!+page.nav]]
</div>

Chunk tplBlogPost

<article class="post">
    <header class="post-header">
        <h3 class="post-title mt0 mb1"><a href="[[~[[+id]]]]">[[+longtitle:default=`[[+pagetitle]]`]]</a></h3>

    [[ImagePlus? 
        &tvname=`image` 
        &docid=`[[+id]]`
        &tpl=`tplBlogIntroImg`
    ]] 

    </header>
    <section class="post-excerpt">
         <p>[[+content:striptags:ellipsis=`255`:typography]]
         <a class="read-more" href="[[~[[+id]]]]">read more »</a></p>
    </section>
    <footer class="post-meta">
        <span class="post-author">[[+createdby:userinfo=`fullname`]]</span>
        <time class="post-date" datetime="[[+publishedon:date=`%B %e, %Y`]]">[[+publishedon:date=`%B %e, %Y`]]</time>
    </footer>
</article>

Chunk tplBlogIntroImg

<div class="feature" style="margin-bottom:1rem">
    <a href="[[~[[+docid]]]]"><img src="[[+source.src:pthumb=`w=320`]]" alt="[[+alt:htmlent]]" /></a>
</div>

items.title: Responsive images
items.text:
If you want to display responsive images with and without the crop, you can use the ImagePlus Snippet.

Snippet Call 

[[ImagePlus? 
&tvname=`yourtvname` 
&options=`&w=320`
&tpl=`tplResponsiveImage`
&pagetitle=`[[*pagetitle]]`
]]

Chunk tplResponsiveImage 

<picture>
    <source media="(min-width: 36em)"
            srcset="[[+source.src:pthumb=`w=1024`]] 1024w,
                [[+source.src:pthumb=`w=640`]] 640w,
                [[+source.src:pthumb=`w=320`]] 320w"
            sizes="33.3vw"/>
    <source srcset="[[+source.src:pthumb=`[[+crop.options]]&w=640`]] 2x,
                [[+source.src:pthumb=`[[+crop.options]]&w=320`]] 1x"/>
    <img src="[[+url]]" alt="[[+alt:default=`[[+pagetitle]]`:htmlent]]"/>
</picture>

items.title: Image formats
items.text:
The image crops are saved in the image format of the Image Format input option of the TV (WebP by default). With the format property of the ImagePlus Snippet, the crop files can be created in other image formats too, i.e. for a picture element with a fallback for older browsers. With an empty tpl property, the snippet returns the URL of the crop file.

Picture element 

<picture>
    <source type="image/avif" srcset="[[ImagePlus? &tvname=`yourtvname` &tpl=`` &format=`avif`]]"/>
    <source type="image/webp" srcset="[[ImagePlus? &tvname=`yourtvname` &tpl=`` &format=`webp`]]"/>
    <img src="[[ImagePlus? &tvname=`yourtvname` &tpl=`` &format=`jpg`]]" alt="[[*pagetitle:htmlent]]"/>
</picture>

The crop files in the other image formats are created on the first output. The AVIF format needs a GD library with AVIF support on the server. Otherwise, the snippet returns the URL of the image and the AVIF source has to be removed.

In a MIGX configuration, the image format of the crop files is set with the format property, i.e. "format":"jpg".

items.title: Create a new template variable
items.text:
Once Image+ is installed, you can create template variables [TV] in the usual way, but instead of setting the Input Type in the Input Options to Image, choose Image+ instead.

For most use cases, you should also set the Output Type in the Output Options to Image+. This allows you to control the image output on a resource.

items.title: The template variable
items.text:
The Image+ TV contains a text field with the path of the image. You can also type or paste the path of an image in the media source of the TV. The triggers on the right side of the field (from left to right):

Trigger Description Clear Removes the image and its image crops from the TV. Crop Opens the cropping window with the first image crop. Upload Uploads an image from your computer into the media source and selects it 1. Browse Opens the media browser of the media source to select an image.

Below the field, the image crops are shown in the order of the Image Crops input option, followed by the original image. Each preview has a bar with the name and the size of the image. The bar of the original image contains a download link. Click on a preview to open the cropping window with that image crop (the original image opens the first image crop). If the TV is less than 700 pixels wide, only the first image crop is shown and the other images are shown, when you hover over it. This compact display can be enabled permanently for each TV by disabling the Show All Images in One Line input option.

The alt text, caption and credits fields are shown below the previews, if they are enabled in the input options of the TV.

items.title: The cropping tool
items.text:
When using an Image+ TV, you can select an image in the same way as you would with a regular Image TV. Once an image is selected, a cropping window will appear where you can select the area of the image to use. The original image is not changed. So you can upload a single image and reuse it in multiple places on the website at different sizes.

The image crops are saved as crop files in the media source. By default they are saved in the crop/ folder, which can be changed with the imageplus.crop_path system setting. They get the image format of the Image Format input option of the TV: WebP (the default), JPEG, PNG, GIF, AVIF or the format of the image.

You can also open the cropping window with the crop trigger (the crop icon) in the image field of the Image+ TV.

In the cropping window you need to drag the handles of the box to change the cropping area. If the TV has been configured with size constraints or an aspect ratio, the cropping area will be limited to that aspect ratio.

You can also change the cropping area with the Left, Top, Width and Height inputs in the Crop Image section below the image. The values are pixels of the original image. A changed value moves or resizes the box, when the input loses the focus or the value is changed with the arrows. A resized box stays centered on its previous position. If the image crop has an aspect ratio, a changed width changes the height too and vice versa. The fields of the original image and the target image only show their sizes and are not editable.

If an image was replaced by a changed image with the same filename, click Reload image in the cropping window. The image is loaded again and all saved image crops are created again from it. If the size of the image has changed, the cropping areas are scaled to the new size. If its aspect ratio has changed, you should check the image crops and save them again. Save the MODX resource afterwards.

  1. The image is uploaded into the path of the Upload Path input option, of the imageplus.upload_path system setting or into the root of the media source. ↩

items.title: Install from MODX Extras
items.text: Search for Image+ in the Package Manager of your MODX installation and install it in there.

items.title: Manual installation
items.text:
If you can't access the MODX Extras Repository in your MODX installation, you can manually install Image+.

  • Download the transport package from MODX Extras (or one of the pre-built transport packages in _packages)
  • Upload the zip file to your MODX installation's core/packages folder or upload it manually in the MODX Package Manager.
  • In the MODX Manager, navigate to the Package Manager page, and select 'Search locally for packages' from the dropdown button.
  • Image+ should now show up in the list of available packages. Click the corresponding 'Install' button and follow the instructions to complete the installation.

items.title: Build it from source
items.text: To build and install the package from source you could use Git Package Management. The GitHub repository of Image+ contains a config.json to build that package locally. Use this option, if you want to debug Image+ and/or contribute bugfixes and enhancements.

items.title: Legacy Image+ 2.x
items.text:
Legacy version

This page contains the documentation of Image+ 2.9.5, the last version before Image+ 3.0. It is only needed for installations, that still use Image+ 2.x. See Update to Image+ 3.x for the migration to the current version.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• MODX Revolution 2.6+
  • PHP 7.1+
  • MODX crop engine i.e. pThumb

The crop engine creates the cropped images. Image+ 2.x supports pThumb, phpThumbOf, phpThumbsUp and phpThumbOn.

items.title: Create a new template variable
items.text:
Once Image+ is installed, you can create template variables [TV] in the usual way, but instead of setting the Input Type in the Input Options to Image, choose Image+ instead.

For most use cases, you should also set the Output Type in the Output Options to Image+. This allows you to control the image output on a resource.

items.title: The cropping tool
items.text:
When using an Image+ TV, you can select an image in the same way as you would with a regular Image TV. Once an image is selected, a cropping window will appear where you can select the area of the image to use. The original image is not changed. So you can upload a single image and reuse it in multiple places on the website at different sizes (and crops with multiple Image+ TVs).

If you want to change the cropping area, you need to click the crop trigger of the Image+ TV.

In the cropping window you need to drag the handles of the dotted box to change the cropping area. If the TV has been configured with size constraints or an aspect ratio, the cropping area will be limited to that aspect ratio.

items.title: Input Options
items.text: In Image+ you can control the final size and aspect ratio of selected images. For an Image+ TV, several advanced input options are available:

items.title: Target Height/Width
items.text: Images can be constrained to a minimum height and/or width with Target Height and Target Width. If both values are set, the target aspect ratio of the output image will be calculated with these values. Both fields must be filled with an integer value.

items.title: Target Aspect Ratio
items.text:
The aspect ratio for the output image can be restricted with Target aspect ratio. If target height and target width are specified, this value is ignored and the calculated aspect ratio of target height and target width is used. The field must be filled with a float value.

If you specify only a value for Target Height or Target Width and leave Target Aspect Ratio blank, the size of the crop is not constrained to any aspect ratio.

How to calculate the aspect ratio

The aspect ratio contains a floating point value: this value can be easily determined by dividing any width with the desired aspect ratio by the corresponding height. For example, suppose you want all your crops to have the same aspect ratio as an image of size "1600x1000", then simply divide "1600" by "1000", which gives the value "1.6". This is the value for your aspect ratio.

items.title: Thumbnail Width
items.text: The width of the thumbnail image in the template variable panel.

items.title: Show Alt Tag Field
items.text:
Image+ TVs can also contain an Alt Tag field which is an additional text input that is stored with each image. It can be output next to the image i.e. as an alt tag or title tag.

To output the alt text in an Image+ TV placeholder, you need to select a chunk in the Output Options. You can also use the ImagePlus snippet and specify a template chunk in the snippet call options. The alt text is entered in the [[+alt]] placeholder in this chunk.

items.title: Show Caption Field
items.text:
Image+ TVs can also include a Caption field, which is an additional text input that is stored with each image. This can be output below the image, i.e. in an additional caption div.

To output the caption in an Image+ TV placeholder, you must select a chunk in the Output Options. You can also use the ImagePlus snippet and specify a template chunk in the call options of the snippet. The caption will be inserted into the [[+caption]] placeholder in that chunk.

items.title: Show Credits Field
items.text:
Image+ TVs can also include a Credits field, which is an additional text input stored with each image. It can be output below the image, for example in an additional credits field.

To output the credits in an Image+ TV placeholder, you must select a chunk in the Output Options. You can also use the ImagePlus snippet and specify a template chunk in the snippet's call options. The credits are inserted into the [[+credits]] placeholder in that chunk.

items.title: Context/System Settings
items.text:
Each Image+ TV Input Option can be replaced by a context or system setting. And context/system settings can be defined for a single TV.

There are predefined system settings in the imageplus namespace which are empty or zero. If you activate one of them or fill it with a value, this setting will override the input options of all Image+ TVs. Context settings must be created before they can be used.

Key Name Description Default imageplus.allow_alt_tag Show Alt Tag Field Allow user to enter a title/alt-tag for the image. No imageplus.allow_caption Show Caption Field Allow user to enter a caption for the image. No imageplus.allow_credits Show Credits Field Allow user to enter a credit for the image. No imageplus.debug Debug Log debug information in the MODX error log. No imageplus.force_config Force predefined crop sizes/aspect ratios Force the usage of predefined crop size/aspect ratios. No imageplus.select_config Predefined crop sizes/aspect ratios Create predefined crop size/aspect ratios that are selectable in the template variable options. [] imageplus.target_height Target Height Constrain the target images to a minimal height. - imageplus.target_ratio Target Aspect Ratio Restrict the target images to a aspect ratio. - imageplus.target_width Target Width Constrain the target images to a minimal width. - imageplus.thumbnail_width Thumbnail Width The thumbnail width of the image in the template variable panel. -

The global context/system settings have the prefix imageplus. and the individual TV context/system settings have the prefix imageplus.{tvname}.. {tvname} must be replaced with the name of the template variable.

The order for these settings is 1:

  • TV name based context setting
  • TV name based system setting
  • context setting
  • system setting

In the imageplus.select_config system setting, you can create predefined crop sizes/aspect ratios with an auxiliary grid. To force the use of the predefined sizes/ratios, you can activate the system setting imageplus.force_config.

items.title: Output Options
items.text: Several advanced output options are available for an Image+ TV:

items.title: Additional phpThumb Parameters
items.text: By default, an Image+ TV returns a relative URL to a cropped (and possibly constrained) image scaled by phpThumb. This output option allows you to assign several additional phpThumb parameters that will be generated to create the thumbnail image.

items.title: Output Chunk
items.text:
When you select an Output Chunk, the TV output is rendered using that chunk. Select the name of the chunk from the drop-down menu. Multiple placeholders are possible in this chunk to customize the output:

Placeholder Description alt Alt text caption Caption credits Credits crop.height Crop height of the thumbnail image crop.options Crop engine crop option string to generate the thumbnail image crop.width Crop width of the thumbnail image crop.x Crop x position of the thumbnail image crop.y Crop y position of the thumbnail image height Minimal height of the thumbnail image options Crop engine full option string to generate the thumbnail image source.height Height of the source image source.src Full path of the source image on the server (not a URL) source.width Width of the source image url URL of the thumbnail image width Minimal width of the thumbnail image

All these placeholders can be used in the Snippet too.

items.title: Generate Thumb URL
items.text:
If you create the thumbnail in the output chunk, i.e. through a pthumb output filter, you can disable the generation of the internal thumb URL.

Caution

You must enable this option if you do not specify an output chunk in the output options or if you use the [[+url]] placeholder in the specified output chunk. Otherwise, the image will not be cropped and the original image path will be returned.

items.title: Thumb URL Issues
items.text: If you use Image+ in a multiple language site with different base URL context settings, you have to set the system setting phpthumbof.cache_url to /. Otherwise, the generated thumbnail path will contain the {base_url} prefix.

items.title: Snippet
items.text:
The snippet gives you a second way to display the TV value. With template variable output you are limited to one output chunk per template variable, with the snippet you can be more flexible and use different output chunks. The following properties can be set in the snippet call:

Property Description Default docid Resource where the Image+ TV value is received from. - options Extended phpThumb options for the image 5. - tpl Template chunk for the snippet output 6. ImagePlus.image tvname Name of the Image+ TV. - type Type of the snippet output. Could be set to check 2, tpl 3 and thumb 4. - value Use this value instead of the TV value, i.e. for a MIGX field. -

items.title: Example
items.text:
[[ImagePlus?
&tvname=`imageplus`
&docid=`1`
&options=`w=100`
&type=`tpl`
&tpl=`ImagePlus.demo`
]]

This snippet call returns the contents of the template variable named imageplus of resource 1 and the extended phpThumb option &w=100 (width: 100px) in the parsed ImagePlus.demo chunk.

items.title: MIGX
items.text:
If you want to use Image+ in MIGX, you can configure all Image+ TV properties with a JSON string in the Configs textarea in the MIGX formtabs field. The following properties are possible:

{
    "targetWidth": "",
    "targetHeight": "",
    "targetRatio": "",
    "thumbnailWidth": "",
    "allowAltTag": "",
    "allowCaption": "",
    "allowCredits": ""
}

You also need to change the Input TV Type to imageplus. You can display the thumbnail in the grid column by setting the renderer to ImagePlus.MIGX_Renderer.

To use this Image+ MIGX field in the frontend, call the ImagePlus Snippet where the value parameter is the name of the MIGX field:

[[ImagePlus?
&value=`[[+migxImagePlusField]]`
]]

Note

The MIGX configs are not migrated by the Image+ 3.0 setup, they have to be changed manually.

  1. The first entry supersedes the second entry in the list etc. ↩

  2. Outputs image if the Image+ TV contains an image, otherwise noimage. ↩

  3. Outputs the parsed template set by the tpl property for the retrieved Image+ TV value (with additional options set by the options property). ↩

  4. Outputs the thumbnail URL for the retrieved Image+ TV value (with additional options set by the options property). ↩

  5. See phpThumb readme for possible options. Maybe not all options are valid in your installation (because of crop engine limitations or server restrictions). ↩

  6. The template chunk placeholders are the same as in the output chunk of the template variable. ↩

items.title: Update to Image+ 3.x
items.text:
The template variable values of Image+ 2.x are converted to the format of Image+ 3.0 by the setup or on their first output.

The setup option Migrate the Image+ 2.x template variables and settings is enabled by default. The migration converts the template variable values to the new value format. It also converts the target width/height input options and settings to the minimal image size input options and to the size of the image crop. At least it converts the target ratio to the ratio of the image crop and removes the legacy settings. The crop files of the image crops are created. Values and crop files, that could not be converted or created, are logged in core/cache/logs/imageplus_migration.log.

items.title: ImagePlusMigration Snippet
items.text:
If you want to check the migration first, disable the setup option and call the ImagePlusMigration snippet uncached on a page, that is only visible for administrators. The snippet output is only shown to manager users, that are sudo users or members of the Administrator user group.

Property Description Default dryRun Report the changes of the migration without saving them. 1

First check the changes:

[[!ImagePlusMigration]]

Migrate afterwards:

[[!ImagePlusMigration? &dryRun=`0`]]

An empty dryRun property keeps the dry run.

items.title: Photos with an EXIF Orientation
items.text: Browsers before 2020 showed photos without their EXIF orientation, so crops of these photos, that were set in such a browser, refer to the photo lying on its side. These crops have to be cropped again.

items.title: Input Options
items.text: In Image+ you can control the final size and aspect ratio of selected images. The image can be selected in the media browser, uploaded or entered as path. After selecting an image, the crop window opens and the image crops can be created. For an Image+ TV, several advanced input options are available:

items.title: Image Crops
items.text:
A JSON encoded object with the image crops of the image. Each crop has a key, a name and one of the following constraints:

Constraint Description Example size The target size of the crop (width x height) 1000x500 proportion The aspect ratio of the crop (width x height) 16x9 ratio Alias of proportion 16x9 width The target width of the crop 800 height The target height of the crop 600 
{
    "desktop": {"name": "Desktop", "size": "1600x800"},
    "mobile": {"name": "Mobile", "proportion": "4x3"}
}

If this option is empty, one image crop without constraints is created.

items.title: Image Format
items.text:
The image format of the image crop files: WebP, JPEG, PNG, GIF, AVIF or the format of the image. The default is WebP, if the GD library of the server supports it, otherwise the format of the image is used. Transparent parts of an image get a white background in a JPEG crop file. The image format must be supported by the GD library of the server, otherwise the crop window shows an error message. A changed image format is used for the image crops, that are saved afterwards. Missing crop files, that are created on the first output, get this image format too.

Option Value WebP webp JPEG jpg PNG png GIF gif AVIF avif Format of the image image

The values are used in the format property of a MIGX configuration. An empty value uses the default.

items.title: Upload Path
items.text: The path in the media source for images, that are uploaded with the upload trigger of the TV. It overrides the imageplus.upload_path system setting. If both are empty, the images are uploaded into the root of the media source. The path can contain the same placeholders as the system setting (see Context/System Settings), i.e. images/[[+year]]/[[+month]]/.

items.title: Minimal Image Width/Height
items.text: The selected or uploaded image must have at least this width and/or height in pixels. Smaller images are rejected with an error message.

items.title: Thumbnail Height
items.text: The height of the preview image in the template variable panel. The default is 250 pixels.

items.title: Show All Images in One Line
items.text: Show the image crops and the original image also in one line, when the template variable panel is at least 700 pixels wide. The default is enabled.

items.title: Show Alt Tag Field
items.text:
Image+ TVs can also contain an Alt Tag field which is an additional text input that is stored with each image. It can be output next to the image i.e. as an alt tag or title tag.

To output the alt text in an Image+ TV placeholder, you need to select a chunk in the Output Options. You can also use the ImagePlus snippet and specify a template chunk in the snippet call options. The alt text is entered in the [[+alt]] placeholder in this chunk.

items.title: Show Caption Field
items.text:
Image+ TVs can also include a Caption Div, which is an additional text input that is stored with each image. This can be output below the image, i.e. in an additional caption div.

To output the caption in an Image+ TV placeholder, you must select a chunk in the Output Options. You can also use the ImagePlus snippet and specify a template chunk in the call options of the snippet. The caption will be inserted into the [[+caption]] placeholder in that chunk.

items.title: Show Credits Field
items.text:
Image+ TVs can also include a Credits field, which is an additional text input stored with each image. It can be output below the image, for example in an additional credits field.

To output the credits in an Image+ TV placeholder, you must select a chunk in the Output Options. You can also use the ImagePlus snippet and specify a template chunk in the snippet's call options. The credits are inserted into the [[+credits]] placeholder in that chunk.

items.title: Context/System Settings
items.text:
The Thumbnail Height, Show Alt Tag Field, Show Caption Field and Show Credits Field input options can be set by a context or system setting. The setting is used, if the input option of the TV is empty. And context/system settings can be defined for a single TV.

There are predefined system settings in the imageplus namespace. Context settings must be created before they can be used.

Key Name Description Default imageplus.allow_alt_tag Show Alt Tag Field Allow user to enter a title/alt-tag for the image. No imageplus.allow_caption Show Caption Field Allow user to enter a caption for the image. No imageplus.allow_credits Show Credits Field Allow user to enter a credit for the image. No imageplus.crop_path Crop Path The path in the media source for the image crop files. crop/ imageplus.debug Debug Log debug information in the MODX error log. No imageplus.thumbnail_height Thumbnail Height The thumbnail height of the image in the template variable panel. Without a value, 250 pixels are used. - imageplus.upload_path Upload Path The path in the media source for uploaded images. -

The upload path and the crop path can contain the placeholders [[+year]], [[+month]], [[+day]], [[+user]], [[+username]], [[+resource_id]] and [[+tv_id]]. The upload path of a single TV is set with the Upload Path input option. The TV name based settings below are not available for the upload path and the crop path.

The global context/system settings have the prefix imageplus. and the individual TV context/system settings have the prefix imageplus.{tvname}.. {tvname} must be replaced with the name of the template variable.

The order for these settings is 1.

  • TV name based context setting
  • TV name based system setting
  • context setting
  • system setting

items.title: Image Output
items.text:
The output uses the image crop files, that are created in the manager. A phpThumb extra is not needed. The URL, the width and the height of the output are the ones of the crop file of the image crop in the Image Crop output option or of the first image crop. If an image crop has no crop file (i.e. a value created before Image+ 3.0), the crop file is created on the first output. Use an image crop with the needed size for each output size.

The format property of the ImagePlus snippet creates the crop files in another image format on the first output. For further image processing, i.e. for different sizes, use the pThumb output filter with the source.src and the options or crop.options placeholders in the output chunk:

<img src="[[+source.src:pthumb=`[[+crop.options]]&w=640&f=webp`]]" alt="[[+alt:htmlent]]">

items.title: Output Options
items.text: Several advanced output options are available for an Image+ TV:

items.title: Additional phpThumb Parameters
items.text: These phpThumb parameters are added to the options placeholder of the output chunk 2. They replace the target size of the image crop in this placeholder and can be used with a pthumb output filter in the output chunk. They don't change the URL of the image crop file.

items.title: Image Crop
items.text: The key of the image crop that is used for the output. If it is empty, the first image crop is used.

items.title: Output Chunk
items.text:
When you select an Output Chunk, the TV output is rendered using that chunk. Select the name of the chunk from the drop-down menu. Multiple placeholders are possible in this chunk to customize the output:

Placeholder Description alt Alt text caption Caption credits Credits crop.height Crop height of the thumbnail image crop.options phpThumb crop option string to generate the thumbnail image crop.url URL of the image crop file stored in the value 6 crop.width Crop width of the thumbnail image crop.x Crop x position of the thumbnail image crop.y Crop y position of the thumbnail image crops.{key}.height Height of the image crop file of the image crop5 crops.{key}.url URL of the image crop file of the image crop5 crops.{key}.width Width of the image crop file of the image crop5 height Height of the image crop file or the image 6 options phpThumb full option string to generate the thumbnail image source.height Height of the source image source.src Full path of the source image on the server (not a URL) source.width Width of the source image url URL of the image crop file or the image 6 width Width of the image crop file or the image 6

All these placeholders can be used in the Snippet too. The crops placeholders are explained in Multiple Image Crops.

items.title: ImagePlus Snippet
items.text:
The snippet gives you a second way to display the TV value. With template variable output you are limited to one output chunk per template variable, with the snippet you can be more flexible and use different output chunks. The following properties can be set in the snippet call:

Property Description Default crop Key of the image crop used for the output. The first image crop is used by default. - docid Resource where the Image+ TV value is received from. Current resource format Image format of the image crop files: jpg, png, gif, webp or avif 7. - options phpThumb options for the options placeholder of the template chunk 2. - source Media source ID, if the value is passed with the value property (i.e. a MIGX value) 4. - tpl Template chunk for the snippet output 3. Without a template chunk, the URL of the image crop file is returned. ImagePlus.image tvname Name of the Image+ TV. - value Image+ value, that is used instead of the TV value, i.e. a MIGX value. -

Media Source

An Image+ value does not contain the media source of the image. The image path and the paths of the crop files are relative to the media source of the template variable. With the tvname property, the snippet uses the media source of the template variable in the context of the resource.

A value passed with the value property (i.e. a MIGX value) has no template variable, so the snippet can't know the media source. In this case it can be set with the source property, when it is not using the default media source. Otherwise, the URLs of the image and its crop files can't be found and missing crop files can't be created.

items.title: Example
items.text:
[[ImagePlus?
&tvname=`imageplus`
&docid=`1`
&options=`w=100`
&tpl=`ImagePlus.demo`
]]

This snippet call returns the contents of the template variable named imageplus of resource 1 in the parsed ImagePlus.demo chunk. The phpThumb option w=100 (width: 100px) is added to the options placeholder.

To check if the template variable contains an image, use an output modifier with an empty template chunk:

[[ImagePlus:notempty=`image`:default=`noimage`?
&tvname=`imageplus`
&tpl=``
]]

items.title: Multiple Image Crops
items.text:
An image can be cropped in several image crops, i.e. for different screen sizes or for a responsive image with different resolutions. The image crops are defined in the Image Crops input option of the TV:

{
    "desktop": {"name": "Desktop", "size": "1600x800"},
    "mobile": {"name": "Mobile", "size": "800x800"}
}

Each image crop is created in the crop window and saved as its own crop file. In the output chunk of the TV and in the template chunk of the snippet, every image crop is available with the crops.{key}.url, crops.{key}.width and crops.{key}.height placeholders. {key} must be replaced with the key of the image crop. The url, width and height placeholders contain the image crop of the Image Crop output option or the crop snippet property.

items.title: Picture Element
items.text:
Different image crops for different screen sizes:

<picture>
    <source media="(max-width: 767px)" srcset="[[+crops.mobile.url]]" width="[[+crops.mobile.width]]" height="[[+crops.mobile.height]]">
    <img src="[[+crops.desktop.url]]" width="[[+crops.desktop.width]]" height="[[+crops.desktop.height]]" alt="[[+alt:htmlent]]">
</picture>

items.title: Responsive Image
items.text:
Image crops with the same aspect ratio in different sizes, i.e. {"small": {"name": "Small", "size": "640x360"}, "large": {"name": "Large", "size": "1280x720"}}:

<img src="[[+crops.large.url]]"
     srcset="[[+crops.small.url]] 640w, [[+crops.large.url]] 1280w"
     sizes="(max-width: 767px) 100vw, 50vw"
     width="[[+crops.large.width]]" height="[[+crops.large.height]]" alt="[[+alt:htmlent]]">

items.title: Snippet
items.text:
Use one of these chunks as template chunk of the snippet:

[[ImagePlus?
&tvname=`imageplus`
&tpl=`ImagePlus.picture`
]]

The URL of a single image crop file is returned with an empty tpl property and the crop property:

[[ImagePlus?
&tvname=`imageplus`
&tpl=``
&crop=`mobile`
]]

Note

A value contains only the image crops, that were saved in the crop window. If an image crop is added to the input option later, its placeholders are empty, until the image crop is saved in the resource. An image path or an Image+ 2.x value contains one image crop 5.

items.title: ImagePlusCleanup Snippet
items.text:
This snippet removes the unused image crop files. Every changed crop is saved as a new file and removed images don't remove their crop files, so the crop folder grows over time.

The crop paths in the values and in the default values of all template variables are used, also in the values of MIGX template variables. The crop files, that the output creates for image crops without a crop file, are used too. All other crop files in the crop folder of the media sources are unused. Only files with the name of a crop file (<image name>-<32 character hash>.<extension>) are regarded. Folders below the crop folder, that are empty afterwards, are removed too. Remote media sources can't be cleaned up.

The snippet output is only shown to manager users, that are sudo users or members of the Administrator user group. All messages are logged in core/cache/logs/imageplus_cleanup.log.

Warning

Crop paths, that are only referenced outside the template variable values (i.e. in a chunk, in a custom database table or in another extra) are not known to the snippet. Check the list of the dry run before removing the files.

Property Description Default dryRun Report the unused crop files without removing them. An empty value keeps the dry run. 1 minAge Skip crop files, that are newer than this number of hours, because a crop is saved before the resource is saved. 24 path Crop folder in the media sources. The part of the imageplus.crop_path system setting before the first placeholder source Comma-separated list of media source IDs. The media sources of the Image+ template variables and the default media source

items.title: Example
items.text:
Call the snippet uncached on a page, that is only visible for administrators. First check the unused files:

[[!ImagePlusCleanup]]

Remove them afterwards:

[[!ImagePlusCleanup? &dryRun=`0`]]

  1. The first entry supercedes the second entry in the list etc. ↩

  2. See phpThumb readme for possible options. Maybe not all options are valid in your installation (because of server restrictions). ↩↩

  3. The template chunk placeholder are the same as in the output chunk of the template variable. ↩

  4. Without the source property, the media source of an Image+ 2.x value or the default media source is used. The media source of the template variable is used with the tvname property. ↩

  5. {key} must be replaced with the key of the image crop. An image path or an Image+ 2.x value contains one image crop with the key of the Image Crop output option or the key crop. ↩↩↩↩

  6. crop.url contains only the URL of an image crop file stored in the Image+ value and is empty otherwise. url, width and height contain the URL and the size of the image crop file, which is created if it is missing. They contain the URL and the size of the image, if the image crop is the unchanged image or if the image crop file could not be created. ↩↩↩↩

  7. Without a value, the image crop files, that were saved in the manager, are used. With another image format, the image crop files are created in that format on the first output. ↩
